hpi_details: A 72-year-old female presents with new-onset wavy distortion of lines (metamorphopsia), which began suddenly and has persisted. She denies generalized systemic symptoms.
ideas: She thinks a tiny blood vessel burst in the back of her eye or that she suffered a silent mini-stroke.
concerns: She is worried that this sudden warping means she will abruptly lose her sight and no longer be able to live independently.
expectations: She hopes to be referred immediately for emergency eye imaging and receive treatment to reverse the distortion.

investigation_events.title: Urgent macular optical coherence tomography
investigation_events.availability_message: The urgent macular OCT result is now available. Retina assessment should proceed promptly.

results.value: Subretinal fluid and pigment epithelial detachment with hyperreflective neovascular material beneath the fovea
results.note: Consistent with active neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Wet (neovascular) age-related macular degeneration evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Wet (neovascular) age-related macular degeneration is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Suspected wet AMD requires urgent retina assessment, with intravitreal anti-VEGF treatment considered after diagnostic confirmation and individualized to disease severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: sudden wavy distortion of lines (metamorphopsia)
Key HPI features: A 72-year-old female presents with new-onset wavy distortion of lines (metamorphopsia), which began suddenly and has persisted.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Wet AMD.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Wet (neovascular) age-related macular degeneration.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Dry AMD without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as new or rapidly progressive metamorphopsia, which requires urgent retina assessment.
management_principles: Arrange urgent retina assessment; anti-VEGF treatment is considered after confirmation of neovascular AMD
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of sudden wavy distortion of lines (metamorphopsia). HPI: wet AMD.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Wet AMD.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Wet AMD.
reference_soap.plan: Arrange urgent retina assessment for OCT and evaluation for neovascular AMD; intravitreal anti-VEGF treatment may be indicated after confirmation. Advise immediate emergency assessment for a curtain-like field loss, new flashes/floaters, or profound sudden vision loss. Counsel patient.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Wet AMD
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Wet AMD
Implement evidence-based management: urgent retina assessment and, if confirmed, intravitreal anti-VEGF treatment

teaching.one_liner: Patient with sudden wavy distortion of lines (metamorphopsia) concerning for wet AMD.
red_flags: New or rapidly progressive metamorphopsia requires urgent retina assessment

must_ask.say: When did the wavy lines first appear—suddenly or over several days?
Is there a blind or dark spot in your central vision?
Have you been diagnosed with macular degeneration before?
Has this gotten noticeably worse in just the past few days?
This needs urgent assessment by a retina specialist; if wet macular degeneration is confirmed, injection treatment may help preserve vision.

It is only in my right eye; when I cover the right eye, my left eye sees straight lines normally.
No, it has been constantly distorted since it began two days ago without coming and going.
Straight lines like door frames and window blinds look bent and wavy, and the center is slightly blurred, but my side vision seems fine.
Reading is much harder because the printed lines look warped, and I have worn the same reading glasses for about two years.
No, I have not noticed any glare, halos around streetlights, or extra trouble driving at night.
No, I haven't seen any floating spots, flashes of light, or dark shadows like a curtain falling.
No, I do not see double images at all.
No, my eyelids are not drooping, and I have no difficulty chewing, swallowing, or speaking.
No, my eye does not hurt at all, even when I move it, and it isn't red.
No, I have no new headaches, no pain when touching my temples, and no jaw ache when chewing.

The distortion appeared suddenly two days ago, and it has stayed prominent without spreading wider.
I thought maybe a little blood vessel popped behind my eye or I had a mini-stroke that made straight doorframes look bent.
I'm terrified that this sudden distortion means I'm going to wake up completely blind and won't be able to live on my own.

Bilateral superficial temporal arteries are non-tender, soft, and normally pulsatile.
